title: Morphology and Distribution of Agglomerates in Enzyme-Stabilized Soil: A Scanning Electron Microscopy Analysis
content: Currently, different chemical additives are used to stabilize soil with the purpose of improve their physical and mechanical properties and obtain the quality required to use them in the construction and building of civil works [1]. One of the most important engineering properties of soil is the compaction, which is directly related to porosity and compression strength [2]. Due to the wide variety of soil types and the many conditions that affect their behavior, there is a need to explore new materials such as chemical stabilizers. Enzyme, for example, have demonstrated the ability to improve adhesion between soil particles [3, 4]. According to this, different techniques are used to analyze soil morphology and microscopy, one of the most widely known and applied is Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), which is used to understand the macroscopic physical and mechanical behavior of soil [5]. The aim of this research project is to apply the enzyme additive Perma-Zyme® base to protease, lipase and chitinase to a clay soil and observe it is effect on soil agglomerates by SEM.
